key_insight: WaspMOT exposes a major blind spot in current multi-object tracking benchmarks: most models are tested on short clips, but real long-term identity preservation is far harder. The benchmark uses long-duration Trichogramma wasp sequences to stress-test tracking over extended time.
problem_solved: Existing MOT datasets often fail to measure whether trackers can keep the same identity across long sequences, occlusions, and appearance changes. WaspMOT addresses this by providing a benchmark built specifically for long-term tracking evaluation in ecological video data.
method: Introduces a benchmark of 10 long sequences of Trichogramma wasps, each around 12,000 frames long.
Captures controlled ecological experiments designed to evaluate persistent identity tracking over many minutes.
Focuses on evaluation rather than model design, providing a testbed for comparing long-term MOT systems.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, WaspMOT offers a more realistic way to measure tracker robustness beyond short, curated sequences. It can reveal failure modes in identity consistency that standard benchmarks miss, especially for applications requiring continuous tracking over time.

paper_title: WaspMOT: A Benchmark for Long-Term Multi-Object Tracking of Trichogramma Wasps
paper_authors: Tomasz Stanczyk, Yuan Gao, Hardik Agarwal, Seongroo Yoon, Tiantao Zhang
